intro: UNESCO's World Heritage List recognises places of outstanding universal value. India's first sites, including the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and the Ajanta and Ellora caves, were inscribed in 1983. As of September 2026, India has 45 World Heritage Sites: 37 cultural, 7 natural and 1 mixed.

The two most recent additions are the Maratha Military Landscapes of India, a group of twelve forts inscribed in July 2025, and the Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath, inscribed in July 2026. The list changes each year, and India also has many more places on UNESCO's Tentative List.
quickAnswer: India has 45 UNESCO World Heritage Sites as of September 2026: 37 cultural, 7 natural and 1 mixed (Khangchendzonga National Park). The first were inscribed in 1983 (the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Ajanta and Ellora). The newest are the Maratha Military Landscapes (2025) and the Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath (2026). Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka and Rajasthan have several sites each.
takeaways: India has 45 World Heritage Sites: 37 cultural, 7 natural and 1 mixed.
The first were inscribed in 1983; the latest is Sarnath, in July 2026.
Ahmedabad (2017) and Jaipur (2019) are inscribed as historic cities.
Several sites span more than one state, such as the Mountain Railways and the Western Ghats.
Most cultural sites are best visited from October to March.

sections.heading: States with the most sites
list: Maharashtra: Ajanta, Ellora, Elephanta, Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus, the Mumbai ensembles and most of the Maratha forts (plus part of the Western Ghats).
Uttar Pradesh: the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri and Sarnath.
Karnataka: Hampi, Pattadakal and the Hoysala temples (plus part of the Western Ghats).
Rajasthan: the Hill Forts, Jantar Mantar, Jaipur City and Keoladeo.
Gujarat: Champaner-Pavagadh, Rani-ki-Vav, Ahmedabad and Dholavira.
Delhi: Humayun's Tomb, the Qutb complex and the Red Fort.

sections.heading: How the list works
paras: Countries nominate sites from their Tentative List, and the World Heritage Committee decides at its annual session. India's Tentative List includes many more places, and new sites have been added almost every year recently. We update this page after each session; check UNESCO's official list for the latest position.

sections.heading: Planning a UNESCO trip
list: Group sites by region: the Golden Triangle, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra's caves, and Karnataka with Tamil Nadu.
Most monuments are managed by the ASI; many sell tickets online.
October to March is the most comfortable season for cultural sites; natural sites follow their own seasons.
Allow half a day or more for large sites such as Hampi, Ellora and Fatehpur Sikri.
after: See how to plan a heritage trip in India for tickets, guides and timing.

safety: Timings, closures and ticket rules are set by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) or the site authority and change from time to time; check the official website before you go, and buy tickets only on official portals.
Do not climb on or touch carvings, and follow the site's rules on photography, drones and tripods.
Weekends and holidays are crowded; arrive at opening time for the calmest visit.
Hire guides at official counters; approved guides carry ASI or state tourism licences.
packing: A light shawl for winter mornings

faqs.q: How many UNESCO World Heritage Sites are there in India?
faqs.a: 45 as of September 2026: 37 cultural, 7 natural and 1 mixed.

faqs.q: What is the newest UNESCO site in India?
faqs.a: The Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath, inscribed in July 2026.

faqs.q: Which Indian cities are UNESCO World Heritage Sites?
faqs.a: The Historic City of Ahmadabad (2017) and Jaipur City (2019); Mumbai's Victorian Gothic and Art Deco ensembles (2018) cover parts of that city.

faqs.q: Which was the first UNESCO site in India?
faqs.a: Agra Fort, the Ajanta Caves, the Ellora Caves and the Taj Mahal were all inscribed in 1983.

faqs.q: Which state has the most UNESCO sites?
faqs.a: Maharashtra has the most sites located fully or partly within it.
